text.p: Exxon Corp's Esso Eastern affiliate and Vietnam's Eastern Investment Co said on Thursday the two companies agreed to a joint venture to build facilities for the distribution and marketing of a broad range of petroleum products.
The venture, Esso East Vietnam Co Ltd, will be 70 percent held by Esso Eastern and 30 percent by Eastern Investment, a commercial enterprise of the Vietnamese government, Exxon said.
The joint venture company will build and operate facilities in Nhabe, Ho Chi Minh City, Exxon said.
Exxon said its facilities in Vietnam will include a modern lube oil blending plant, an liquified petroleum gasoline plant and a bulk asphalt plant.

A cost estimate for the venture has not yet been determined, a company spokeswoman said. The spokeswoman said Exxon would have a better idea about the costs after the engineering work had been completed.
Exxon said its Esso branded lubricants are now available through Vietnam's distribution network and it is supplying various Vietnamese parties with fuels and asphalt from Singapore.

Eastern Investment holds interests in a wide range of business operations that include real estate investment, construction materials, hotels and restaurants, warehousing, import-export and general services.
